name: coordinator-lifecycle-exclusivity
body:
Session lifecycle and exclusivity. `apg session start` launches the coordinator; `apg session end` flushes and exits cleanly; one session per worktree DB (a second start refuses or joins, never a second writer). A crash leaves a stale socket, which the next command/session cleans up (no live process behind it).

Mid-request session death: if the session dies after accepting a forwarded mutation but before committing/responding, the client MUST NOT silently fall back to the direct path — that could double-apply a mutation that already landed. Each forwarded mutation carries a client-generated request id; the coordinator records applied ids so a replay after reconnect is idempotent (apply-once). On a transport error the client reports the failure and the mutation id to the caller so the state can be reconciled, and only retries when the coordinator is reachable again and can confirm the id was not applied. The outcome is never hidden and never silently re-applied.

Read-only openers: `apg query` and every suite query tool open `db.lbug` read-only (`read_only(true)`, src/main.rs:963). While a session is live they must keep working unchanged (transparency): a read-only open that does not take lbug's exclusive lock is safe concurrently with the session's writer; any that would contend waits (or routes through the session). The session must never hold the DB in a state that blocks a read.

A session is exclusive with `apg scan` and `apg project merge`, which replace `db.lbug` (the session flushes/ends first, or those refuse while a session is live). Acceptance: start→mutations→end round-trips; a killed session leaves no process holding the DB and its stale socket is reclaimed; a mutation forwarded to a dying session is applied at most once and the client reports (never hides) the outcome; `apg query` / suite reads work while a session is live; scan/merge and a live session never contend.
